questions.question: Practical station: Gram stain.

parts.text: Vaginal smear — describe the smear and give your interpretation.
In a patient with COPD, what would be the most likely organism?

parts_raw.text: In a COPD patient, what would be the most likely organism?

questions.model_answer:
a) Vaginal smear: numerous squamous epithelial cells with an abundant, predominant population of large gram-positive bacilli (lactobacilli), few or no small pleomorphic gram-variable coccobacilli, no clue cells, few leukocytes; budding yeast cells with pseudohyphae are present. Interpretation: Nugent score 0–3, normal lactobacillus-predominant flora — no evidence of bacterial vaginosis; yeast present, consistent with vulvovaginal candidiasis (culture to confirm Candida species).
b) Sputum: abundant polymorphonuclear leukocytes (>25 per low-power field) with rare/few squamous epithelial cells (<10 per LPF) — an acceptable lower-respiratory specimen (Q score satisfactory) — showing a predominance of small gram-negative coccobacilli/bacilli.
c) Haemophilus influenzae (non-typeable) — the most likely organism in an acute exacerbation of COPD with small pleomorphic gram-negative coccobacilli on Gram stain.

cohort_answer.text: Vaginal smear: No BV. Yeast present. Sputum smear: ++WBC, rare epithelial cells, +GNB.

questions.question: An older man with COPD (or, in the pediatric exam, a 26-week-old infant) presents with an upper respiratory tract infection after contact with a 2-year-old who had a cold.
questions.question_raw: URTI in old guy with COPD (or a 26 week old baby in peds exam) in contact with a 2 year old who had a cold

parts.text: What diagnostic test will give a result within 24 hours?

parts_raw.text: What diagnostic test will give result within 24 hrs?

questions.model_answer: a) Reverse-transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR), ideally as a multiplex respiratory viral panel on a nasopharyngeal swab/wash; it is more sensitive than rapid antigen testing and returns results the same day. b) (1) RSV; (2) Influenza virus; (3) Parainfluenza virus; (4) Rhinovirus; (5) Human metapneumovirus; (6) Adenovirus (coronavirus is an acceptable sixth).

cohort_answer.text: Diagnostic test: RPP (respiratory pathogen panel). Viruses: Influenza; Rhinovirus; Parainfluenza; RSV; Human metapneumovirus; Adenovirus.
